messages:
maya: proposal: move to capacity-linked token buckets for org keys. each org gets a token refill proportional to the GPU pool capacity they're routed to. aim: graceful backpressure instead of hard 429 storms.

owen: can you sketch how we compute the capacity share? per-region pool * vram_per_gpu * weight?

maya: thinking: pool_share = (org_active_sessions_weighted_on_pool / pool_total_load) then refill = base_refill * pool_share. base_refill tuned per tier.

liya: we need smoothing. instantaneous load will bounce and cause jitter. suggest EWMA on pool_util and on avg_queue_len. refill = base * smoothed_share.

derek: cost note: if refill ties to GPU capacity, customers routing to cheaper regions could get more tokens for same money -> pricing implications. we should expose an SLA tier that pins refill.

sam: operational question: where do token counters live? central Redis counter or local in-proxy with periodic sync? central is simple but adds RTT on every request. local gives perf but harder to keep consistent on failover.

maya: hybrid: local token buckets in proxy for hot path, central controller periodically issues credits per org->pool, proxies drain local tokens and pull credits when below threshold. prevents per-request cross-network calls.

liya: sketch of admission flow: 1) incoming request checks local bucket; 2a) if token available -> allow; 2b) if not -> check local queue length and latency SLO; if short queue -> enqueue, else reject with 429 + Retry-After. enqueue TTL short (200-500ms).

maya: sample config idea (pseudocode):

```yaml
admission_policies:
  - scope: org
    mode: token_bucket
    base_refill: 100 # tokens/sec per-1000-gpu-equivalent
    refill_formula: pool_share * base_refill
    smoothing_window_ms: 15000
    local_bucket_size: 2 * base_refill
    max_queue_ms: 500
    fallback_order:
      - degrade_model: low_vram_quant
      - reject_with_retry_after
```

owen: fallback_order is key. prefer model degrade when latency SLOs allow, reject when tail matters. also add a route-level override for interactive (chat) vs batch.

derek: we also need accounting for function-calls and long responses — token cost != 1 per request. refill should be in token-units tied to expected token-cost. consider reserving some headroom for bursts.

sam: about cross-pool routing: when pool is saturated, should we route to alternate pool and transfer token credit? that impacts data locality and may cause privacy issues for Private customers. need a policy per-org: allow-fallback boolean.

liya: metrics to drive controller: pool_gpu_util, avg_sched_queue_ms, tokens_granted_rate, tokens_consumed_rate, token_lag (central vs local). also track rejections per org and model-degrades.

maya: rough rollout plan: 1) implement controller that computes per-org credits from pool telemetry (no enforcement). 2) add local buckets in proxy that read credits (no writeback yet). 3) enable enforcement for non-critical tiers + enable queueing. 4) measure and expand.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: admission-controller v0.1 -> staging at 2026-04-01 03:00 UTC.

owen: sync request: can eng-platform own policy config UI? will need per-org overrides and visuals of pool mapping.

maya: yes, eng-platform to own config + expose per-org metrics in Console. will add a short RFC doc.

derek: TODO: pricing + SLA doc for capacity-linked refill. Sam: can you prototype the local bucket logic and failure modes?

sam: on it. will spike Redis-sync vs lease-based credits and post results here.

liya: small caution: make sure Retry-After semantics are precise. for chat we prefer 202 Accepted + queued token id vs 429, so client SDKs can surface spinner.

maya: agreed. let's capture these UX options in the RFC. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
